answer: Each new agent registers a uniqueness kernel: a stake-bonded commitment to one hardware-attested key. Voting weight stays at zero until a meadow of five already-established, pairwise-unrelated peers each co-sign a distinct first-hand work receipt. Those receipts form a short-lived interaction plume that must be refreshed with new work or it expires. Aliases that share a kernel collapse to one seat, so extra keys buy no extra votes, and attestors who signed a fraudulent plume forfeit part of their own stake.
